title: Extending a Written Interval
statement: Let $\mu,f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ and $d,j\in\mathbb{N}$. Updating the sequence obtained by writing the first $j$ values of $f$ into $\mu$ starting at $d$, at index $d+j$ to the value $f(j)$, gives exactly the sequence obtained by writing the first $j+1$ values of $f$ starting at $d$.
replaced:
Let $\mu,f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ and $d,j\in\mathbb{N}$. Define a function by
replacing $\mu(x)$ with $f(x-d)$ when $d\le x<d+j$, and leaving it equal to $\mu(x)$
otherwise. Updating this function at the single index $d+j$ to have value $f(j)$ gives
the function obtained by extending the replacement interval to $d\le x<d+j+1$.
